title: Observation of giant nonvolatile magneto-thermal switching in superconductor-ferromagnet hybrids
authors: Yui Sakamoto, Fuyuki Ando, Keigo Ito, Hossein Sepehri-Amin, Takamasa Hirai, Yuto Watanabe, Poonam Rani, Yoshikazu Mizuguchi, Ken-ichi Uchida
abstract: Magneto-thermal switch is a crucial thermal component which enables heat transfer control by the application of an external magnetic field. Recently, a nonvolatile behavior in magneto-thermal conductivity at zero magnetic field was observed in type-II and phase-separated superconductors owing to magnetic flux pinning nature, leading to an energy-efficient thermal control technology. However, the nonvolatile magneto-thermal switching ratio has been much lower than the volatile one in conventional materials. Here, we demonstrate a giant nonvolatile magneto-thermal switching in ferromagnetic Fe-superconducting Pb hybrids. The dispersion of pure Fe particles realizes increased electron and decreased phonon contributions in the thermal conductivity, which enhances the magneto-thermal switching ratio at the superconducting-to-normal conducting phase transition. Furthermore, in concert with trapped magnetic flux by supercurrent, ferromagnetic moment of Fe breaks the superconductivity of Pb matrix at zero magnetic field, enabling a significantly large nonvolatility even with a slight amount of Fe inclusions. Consequently, the nonvolatile magneto-thermal switching ratio reaches 719% in maximum at the Fe ratio of 8.7 vol%, which is more than twice the previous record value observed in Pb-Sn composites and the volatile one in pure Pb. This work broadens the exploration space and strategy for giant nonvolatile magneto-thermal switching materials.
summary: This work reports on achieving a record-high giant nonvolatile magneto-thermal switching ratio using Pb-Fe superconductor-ferromagnet hybrids. The enhancement is attributed to the ferromagnetic inclusions creating strong magnetic pinning centers that break superconductivity at zero field. This demonstrates a highly promising strategy for next-generation, energy-efficient thermal management materials.
main_problem: To develop an energy-efficient thermal control component by achieving a giant nonvolatile magneto-thermal switching ratio (MTSR).
main_result: The authors achieved a record-high nonvolatile MTSR of 719% in ferromagnetic Fe-superconducting Pb hybrids, significantly surpassing previous records.
method: Thermal conductivity ($\kappa$) was measured as a function of external magnetic field ($H$) before and after cycling the field to quantify the nonvolatility. Sample preparation involved accumulative roll bonding (ARB).
model_or_system: The study investigates superconductor-ferromagnet hybrids, specifically Pb-Fe systems, where the ferromagnetic moment of Fe interacts with the superconducting state of Pb.
key_observables: Thermal conductivity ($\kappa$), Nonvolatile MTSR, Remanent Magnetization ($4\pi M_r$).
important_parameters: Fe inclusion ratio (varied), Temperature (2.0 K), Magnetic Field ($H$).
main_assumptions: The nonvolatility is attributed to the ferromagnetic moment of Fe breaking superconductivity at zero field, leading to trapped magnetic flux effects.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate schematics of MTS, elemental mapping confirming Fe dispersion in Pb, and plots showing $\kappa$ vs $H$, MTSR vs inclusion ratio for both Fe and Sn systems, and magnetization vs temperature/field history.
paper_structure: The paper details the fabrication process (ARB), characterization (SEM-EDX), measurement of thermal conductivity dependence on $H$ to show MTS, quantification of nonvolatility using $\kappa_{ini}$ vs $\kappa_{fin}$, and correlation between MTSR and remanent magnetization.
why_interesting: The strong coupling between magnetism (ferromagnetism) and superconductivity in the presence of thermal transport mechanisms provides a platform for studying coupled order parameters, relevant to non-equilibrium quantum phenomena.
